title: What is AWS for .NET Developers
description: See how AWS services fit into ASP.NET Core and C# development workflows.

data.text: **Amazon Web Services (AWS)** is a cloud platform that lets .NET developers host apps, store data, secure secrets, and monitor production systems without managing physical servers.

data.title: Benefits for C# developers
items: **First-class .NET SDKs** — AWS services ship with idiomatic C# client libraries
**Native Visual Studio tooling** — publish, debug, and monitor AWS apps from the IDE
**Global infrastructure** — run apps close to users in dozens of regions
**Broad service catalog** — compute, storage, databases, AI, and more

data.title: C# First
data.text: Most AWS services expose async-first, Task-based C# client libraries. You will see `async Task` and `await` throughout this course because AWS operations are almost always network calls.

terms.definition: A geographic area containing multiple isolated data centers called Availability Zones.
A set of NuGet packages that provides idiomatic C# client libraries for AWS services.

data.title: Call Amazon S3 from C#
data.content: AWS SDK methods use standard .NET patterns like async/await and `using` for disposables. This example includes error handling and a cancellation token.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: AWS provides managed services for hosting, storage, data, caching, and monitoring
AWS SDK for .NET gives you idiomatic C# client libraries
Visual Studio integrates with AWS for development and deployment
Most AWS operations in C# are async because they call cloud services over HTTP
data.takeaway: Think of AWS as an extension of your C# toolbox: instead of building infrastructure yourself, you call AWS SDK methods from your existing code.
